doc.title: Louis Hayes interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000

title: Composing by singing into a tape recorder, a tune for his wife
summary: He composes in his head, sang the tune into a recorder, Ronnie Matthews wrote it out, and his wife doubted he wrote it.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Wow. I have one little piece of music to play here.
That’s what I just mentioned to you.
Now as a composer, do you sit at the piano and work out things?
No actually, I wish I could actually. But my piano facilities are not that great. So I put this tune together in my head and I sang it in a tape recorder.
I love that. That’s great, yeah.

And it gave me, I mean that was a job. I mean I had this record date so I wanted to think of something. And my wife and myself naturally we were close as could be. But sometimes we would have little problems, as men and women when you’re married, so I’m trying to do something and think of something to help get me out of this, on the good side. So I had to think of this, I had to write this composition and dedicate it to my wife, very important. So I sat there on the couch and I started putting this together. And I put it together and after I got it in my head and I sang it in this machine, I went to the pianist at the time Ronnie Matthews, and I explained it to him, and he made music out of it, put the chord changes to it, and that’s how it came about. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -13-
That’s great. I don’t wish any more arguments on you but if you come up with tunes, maybe the good times could lead to a tune too.
Yeah my wife after she heard it she said “you didn’t write it, you didn’t write that.” So I had to go and get that original singing and whistling I was doing.
It came from this kind of raw inspiration and look what came out of it.
Yes. So after that she bought me this little thing, this little machine that I can just click it on and when I have an idea right there, just sing right in to it.
